newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nobel peace laureate attacks Malaysia, Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Nobel peace laureate attacks Malaysia, Indonesia.

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta on Thursday accused Malaysia and Indonesia of declaring "war" on the U.N. Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
The East Timorese independence leader also rejected the argument that Asia has a different concept of human rights than the rest of the world.

"There are those in power, particularly in this region of the world, who are attempting to derail the gains made by the international community, to roll back the freedoms won by humanity in the last century," Horta said in a speech on human rights at the University of New South Wales.

"In the recent meeting of ASEAN countries and their Western partners in Kuala Lumpur, Prime Minister Mahathir of Malaysia and Indonesian Foreign Minister Alatas declared war on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights," Horta said.
"Both claimed that this profound and historic document...is merely a minority viewpoint," said the co-winner of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize.

Malaysian Prime Minister Mohamed Mahathir last month called for a review of the 1948 human rights declaration. Malaysian media has said Mahathir believes the document was the product of the major powers of that era and was no longer suitable.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas last month said a review did not mean a dilution of human rights. But the calls for a review prompted the United States to warn that it would vigorously oppose any dilution of the declaration.
Horta said the argument that human rights in Asia was somehow different from the rest of the world was a discredited argument once used by the former Soviet Union.
"Asia, they say, has a concept of human rights and cultural values that is different from those of Europe, Latin America and Africa," Horta said.

"This argument has been appropriated by certain Asian regimes: a mixed bag of military dictatorships, Islamic autocrats with a perverse interpretation of the Koran, and the last of the remaining Stalinist dinosaurs."
Horta said democratic governments must unite to "defeat this ridiculous notion and advance the cause of universal human rights".
He said there had been significant advances in human rights in the past 50 years and a greater awareness of human rights.
"The movement for democracy, human rights and rule of the law if irreversible," he said.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after Portugal had abandoned the colony, and annexed the territory in 1976. The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian sovereignty over East Timor.
